headline: Common Mistakes to Avoid During House Fire Cleanup
articleBody:
When your home has been hit by a fire, the aftermath can be chaotic, and it's easy to make choices that could complicate the recovery process. Knowing what *not* to do is just as important as knowing what *to* do, especially when you're dealing with sensitive fire and smoke damage. 

One big mistake people make is re-entering the property too soon. Always wait for the fire department to declare it safe; structural integrity might be compromised, or hazardous fumes could linger. Another common error is using regular household cleaners on smoke and soot. These aren't designed for fire residue and can actually spread the soot, embed the smell deeper, or even permanently stain surfaces. You definitely don't want to discard items prematurely either. Many things that look ruined can actually be restored by professionals using specialized techniques, saving you money and heartache. And here’s a crucial one: delaying professional help. Smoke and soot are corrosive; the longer they sit, the more damage they inflict. Waiting can mean the difference between restoration and replacement for many items. Don't try to power wash or wet-clean everything right away; certain materials need specific cleaning methods to prevent further damage. If you're unsure, it's always best to consult with experts.
